EV Interconnect: Battery pack cell-to-cell interconnections evaluated in the model for aluminum substitution, balancing a ~42% mass reduction and lower BOM cost against laser welding and reliability penalties.
EV Busbar: Rigid high-current powertrain conductors evaluated in the model primarily for high mass savings and direct material cost reduction through aluminum substitution.
Wire Harness: Vehicle power and signal wiring networks evaluated in the model based on total vehicle mass impact, bundle diameter limits, and architectural redesign requirements.
EV Traction Motor Winding: Stator electromagnetic coils evaluated in the model under strict volumetric packing and power-density limits that heavily favor copper's high electrical conductivity.
ICE Busbar: Conventional vehicle distribution channels evaluated in the model for bulk power routing where mass reduction carries a lower premium than in battery-electric vehicles.
ICE Wire Harness: Low-voltage auxiliary wiring assemblies evaluated in the model for trade-offs among material cost, harness flexibility, and vehicle assembly constraints.
ICE Alternator: Windings Generator rotor and stator coils evaluated in the model under engine-bay thermal constraints and tight physical volume limits that demand high conductivity.
Commercial HVAC: Heavy-duty heat exchangers and motor coils evaluated in the model balancing physical footprint, operating pressures, thermal performance, and corrosion risks.
Residential HVAC: Residential air conditioning and heat pump coils evaluated in the model where lower unit manufacturing cost is weighed against long-term warranty and leak reliability risks.
Distribution Lines: Medium-voltage utility cables evaluated in the model where flexible trench rights-of-way allow larger aluminum conductor sizes to minimize overall project cost.
Transmission Line: High-voltage bulk power conduits evaluated in the model under tight duct size constraints and high current loads that favor high-conductivity copper.
Solar Array: Cables Outdoor direct-current cabling evaluated in the model based on cable weight, cost per meter over long run distances, and terminal connection reliability.
